activities.title: The direction matters
activities.instruction: Trace data through a component tree and decide where values and handlers should live.

content.title: Design the Data Flow
content.hook: In the React model you have been building:
content.context:
**parent state/data → props → child UI**

And interaction often travels back upward through a function prop:

**child event → handler prop → parent state update → new props → new UI**

This gives the component tree a direction.
goals: Trace data through a component tree and decide where values and handlers should live.

options.text: It came from data owned higher in the tree and moved down through props.

feedback.correct: Data flows through explicit props. The farther you trace upward, the closer you get to its owner.
feedback.incorrect: Data flows through explicit props. The farther you trace upward, the closer you get to its owner.

content.title: Interaction flows back
content.text:
Now suppose `Row` needs to tell the parent that the user selected it.

```jsx
<Row onSelect={() => setSelectedId(2)} />
```

And inside `Row`:

```jsx
<button onClick={onSelect}>Select</button>
```

The child does not directly reach into the parent's state.

It calls the capability the parent gave it.

options.text: “Children can change any parent's state whenever they want.”
“A parent can pass a function that gives a child a specific capability.”

feedback.correct: The second explanation preserves the component boundary. The child knows what it can request, not every detail of how the parent stores state.
feedback.incorrect: The second explanation preserves the component boundary. The child knows what it can request, not every detail of how the parent stores state.

content.question:
Suppose two sibling components must always agree on which tab is selected.

Where should the selection live?

options.text: In their closest common parent, then pass the value and handlers down.

feedback.correct: One source of truth is easier to coordinate than duplicate selection state.
feedback.incorrect: One source of truth is easier to coordinate than duplicate selection state.

content.question:
You have:

```text
App
 ├─ SearchBox
 └─ ProductList
      └─ ProductRow
```

The search text determines which products appear.

Where is the strongest place for the search text to live?

feedback.correct: Both `SearchBox` and `ProductList` need the value, so their closest useful common owner is `App`.
feedback.incorrect: Both `SearchBox` and `ProductList` need the value, so their closest useful common owner is `App`.

content.question: A component should usually own state when:

options.text: It is the only part of the tree that needs the state.
State must be shared by many components.
It is the deepest component in the tree.

feedback.correct: Keep state as local as practical. Move it upward when coordination requires a shared owner.
feedback.incorrect: Keep state as local as practical. Move it upward when coordination requires a shared owner.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Data has an owner. Props carry it down. Events or callbacks communicate intent back up.
**Senior habit:** When state feels difficult, draw the component tree and circle the smallest component that can own the source of truth.
